extractor.note: Read every paragraph carrying transcend- (outside transcendental), immanen-, surpass or going beyond, in file order, with its section. Later marginal revisions the commentary reports are recorded under the 1910/11 stratum because the commentary does not date them.

coverage_note: Term-led pass over the whole file (lines 1-419): every paragraph containing the transcendence family, including bare transcendent and immanent, was read in full; paragraphs without any such word were not read.

units.claim: The synopsis of the course names among its problems transcendence within immanence, the several concepts of transcendence, and the right of transcendent positing within immanence.
units.quote: transcendence within immanence and the several distinct concepts of transcendence; the right (Recht, the warrant or legitimacy) of transcendent positing within immanence

units.claim: The in-itself being of the experienced thing remains forever pretension, since it is never given absolutely, and this hangs together with experience positing transcendence by its very sense.
units.quote: And this hangs together with the fact that experience, by its very sense, posits transcendence.

units.claim: The new phenomenological attitude switches off every empirical, transcendent attitude and accepts no object posited in it as actuality.
units.quote: We can give ourselves, quite generally, a new kind of attitude that switches off every empirical, transcendent attitude.

units.claim: Solipsism arises from a misunderstanding of the proper sense of transcendence and its switching-off, which mistakes psychological immanence for phenomenological immanence.
units.quote: a misunderstanding of the proper sense of transcendence and of its switching-off leads one to mistake psychological immanence — which is the solipsistic one, the immanence of my mental states within my worldly soul — for phenomenological immanence

units.claim: The past of the perception transcends the now, so that switching it off by analogy with the empirically transcendent would leave nothing to judge.
units.quote: The past transcends the now, and so, it seems, I must switch it off, analogously to the empirically transcendent.

units.claim: Admitting retention, and not only it but that of which it is retention, admits a transcendence within the phenomenological attitude.
units.quote: Therewith we have admitted a "transcendence" within the phenomenological attitude: insofar as we admit not only the retention itself as phenomenological being, but also that of which it is retention.

units.claim: Admitting that the perception remembered in recollection in fact was yields new transcendences within phenomenological immanence, which are not absolute indubitabilities.
units.quote: With this, Husserl says, we would have new "transcendences" within the phenomenological immanence

units.claim: The phenomenological reduction yields an abundance of intuitive connections beheld in other manners than phenomenological perception, so there is throughout transcendence in the phenomenological immanence and the possibility of deception.
units.quote: Throughout, there is "transcendence in the phenomenological immanence," and throughout, the possibility of deception.

units.claim: Transcendence in the general sense that the cognition-object is not itself present in the act belongs to every intentional relation, and in that respect one does not speak of transcendence lest immanence lose its sense.
units.quote: In this respect, however, one does not speak of "transcendence," for then the opposite term "immanence" would lose all sense.

units.claim: In the second sense immanence is only what is bodily present to a beholding, and everything non-present stands on the side of transcendence, including what a reduced recollection reproduces.
units.quote: On the side of immanence, in this second sense, stands only the beheld

units.claim: In the third sense immanence and transcendence divide individual objects into the beholdable and those given only through appearances, and nature belongs on the side of transcendence.
units.quote: On the side of transcendence, in this third sense, belongs precisely nature — for "nature" is just the title encompassing the totality of objectivities that present themselves through appearances.

units.claim: Phenomenology does not want to switch off transcendence in every sense, only transcendence in the sense of the appearing, that is, nature.
units.quote: phenomenology does not want to switch off transcendence in every sense. From the very outset it was defined by the switching-off of nature — of transcendence in a determinate sense, transcendence in the sense of the appearing

units.claim: The all-embracing phenomenological reduction switches off all transcendence in the sense of natural existence-positing without doubting it.
units.quote: we switch off all transcendence in the sense of natural existence-positing

units.claim: Wherever natural experience posits a transcendent unity, its existence is bracketed but the positing serves as an index for determinate pure connections of consciousness.
units.quote: wherever natural experience posits a transcendent unity — an existing real thing, a real constellation, an existing process of change, whether in present, past, or future — there this existence is indeed bracketed

units.claim: Psychophysical cognition is natural cognition only through its interweaving with physical natural cognition, called transcendent cognition, and stands as an intermediate member.
units.quote: which is properly natural cognition only through its interweaving with genuine, physical natural cognition (transcendent cognition)

absences.expected_because: The other I is attained through double reduction and nature becomes an index of coordinated monads, extending the formula of §35 that turns the transcendent unity into an index.
The section restates the abstention from every judgment about the being of nature, which §30 defined as the switching-off of transcendence in a determinate sense.
